evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 注音; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry reports that Shuowen’s headform for 票 was 𤐫, glossed “fire flying,” and says its lower 火 became 示 through clerical change. It records two modern Mandarin readings, piāo and piào. The cited Han shu passages and Tang commentaries describe shaking, light movement, and nimbleness; separate later examples show paper money and documentary credentials, including a Qing salt-administration example. These examples do not establish a continuous semantic path from fire to tickets or paper money.
evidence.title: [A02895] 票 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》; lexical examples
evidence.text: The entry describes 票 as written earlier 𤐫, with upper [𦥑囟] and lower 火; it says the upper part was reduced to 覀 and 火 was confused with 示 in the clerical form. It reports the basic sense as fire rising, followed by light movement and rapidity. It cites a Shuihudi Qin daybook slip 57 example 票風 (“rapid wind”), Han shu examples, and Ming-period documentary uses. The entry does not independently identify the upper element’s referent or prove a dated chain linking the fire sense to documents.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies 𤐫 as an older form associated with 票 and cites Shuowen, Guangyun, and Zhengzitong descriptions. Its notes support the reported graphic relationship, but do not establish the upper element as paired hands, a bag, a basket, or sparks.
evidence.title: [A02895-002] 𤐫 (票) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 葛希谷, Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: 論證：睡虎地秦墓竹簡《日書》甲種《盜者》篇“票行”
evidence.text: The article surveys competing readings of a separate Shuihudi phrase 票行 and argues for reading 票 as 少. This dispute means 票行 should not be treated as secure evidence for a rapid-motion sense; it does not negate the separate 票風 example cited by CUHK.

gaps: No verified oracle-bone or bronze attestation for 票/𤐫 was established in this pass; a displayed inventory of seal and bamboo-slip examples is not proof that earlier forms did not exist.

The upper graphic element [𦥑囟] is not independently identified as a particular object or action. The dossier’s paired-hands, bag/basket, sparks, and altar explanations remain unsupported by the inspected references.
No phonetic component is established by the inspected sources. The readings of 火 and 票 are recorded separately; they do not establish a historical sound relationship.

The fire-to-light-movement/rapidity connection is presented in dictionary accounts, but a continuous dated semantic development is not demonstrated. CUHK reports 票風 on a Qin slip; the distinct phrase 票行 has disputed readings.

The earliest attestation for paper slips, credentials, tickets, or ballots was not established. The inspected dictionaries give Ming-era documentary examples and later paper-money examples, but dictionary ordering does not establish chronology.
Both official Unicode Unihan character-specific endpoints attempted for 票 and 火 were inaccessible. Their supplied local reading rows are not externally verified here.

The exact Commons file’s identity description and public-domain terms were verified, but its SVG pixels were not visually inspected in this pass. Its description makes it a modern reconstruction, not an artifact image.
No reuse assessment for bulk or repeated source material was made; only character-specific paraphrases were used.
